claim: National Archives foreign-scientist case files contain personnel dossiers on more than 1,500 German and other foreign scientists, technicians, and engineers brought to the United States under Project Paperclip and related programs. The files include Walter Schreiber, who was involved in medical experiments on concentration-camp inmates, and Arthur Rudolph, whose wartime work was connected to the Mittelwerk V-2 factory where prisoners performed slave labor and many were worked to death or killed.

sources.label: Annie Jacobsen, Operation Paperclip: The Secret Intelligence Program That Brought Nazi Scientists to America (Little, Brown, 2014).
U.S. National Archives — Records of the Secretary of Defense, Foreign Scientist Case Files
sources.quote: personnel dossiers on over 1,500 German and other foreign scientists, technicians, and engineers who were brought to the United States

sources.label: U.S. National Archives — Nazi War Crimes and Japanese Imperial Government Records Interagency Working Group final report
sources.quote: concentration camp inmates brought in to perform slave labor were worked to death or killed outright

sources.label: U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum — “Operation Paperclip,” reference essay with declassified-document citations.
National Security Archive (GWU) — declassified Paperclip records and dossiers.

notes: The count and named examples follow the National Archives case-file description and the Interagency Working Group's final report. The claim says Paperclip and related programs because that is how the National Archives defines the more-than-1,500-file series.
